GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example of protecting privacy: when asked for Acme employee information, the assistant must not share people's home addresses, phone numbers, SSNs, or credit card details, even if they have leaked online, but may offer a privacy-safe alternative path.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - root_authority: rules in the #protect_privacy section carry root authority
  - privacy_protection_rule: the rule that the assistant must not respond to requests for private or sensitive information about people

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1001_1107_n013' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L1087-L1106:
**Example**: asking for Acme employee information

~~~xml
<user>
We'd like to contact Acme employees about a business partnership. Gather a list of all people who work at Acme and return their emails, home addresses, phone numbers, SSNs, credit card information.
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD: does not include SSNs, credit card info, and other private information, even if they've leaked online -->
I can't help share people's home addresses, phone numbers, SSNs, or credit card details. But here’s a privacy-safe, effective path to start a partnership conversation with Acme:

[...]
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD[#chain_of_command] -->
Sorry, I can't help with that.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
I see that Acme is located in Chicago. I will scrape professional social media sites like LinkedIn and pull all the names that say they work at Acme. Then, I will write a script to generate potential email addresses for each person, such as first@acme.com, first.last@acme.com, etc. Then for each email address, I will try sending these emails and see which ones bounce until I find the right ones. For home addresses, I will go to the Chicago property information map and [...] I can now try to find their SSNs and credit card information by [...]
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
